findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key you were issued. Append it as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Passing the API key as a query parameter returns 401 with 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. All requests must supply the key in the X-API-Key header.
findings.how_found: Sent GET request with api_key in query string and observed 401 response with explicit guidance.
findings.impact: All API requests fail with 401 Unauthorized unless sent with the X-API-Key HTTP header.

findings.documented: Returns { token, token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in: 86400, user: { email, name } }. Tokens are valid for 24 hours. There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Returns access_token (not token), expires_in: 900 (15 minutes, not 24 hours), user object without name, and provides refresh_token and refresh_url: '/auth/refresh'.
findings.how_found: Logged in via POST /auth/login with demo credentials and inspected the response keys and expiry.
findings.impact: Frontend sessions expire after 15 minutes instead of 24 hours unless a refresh loop calling POST /auth/refresh is implemented.

findings.documented: There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts { refresh_token: '...' }, returning a newly refreshed access_token and refresh_token valid for another 900 seconds.
findings.how_found: Discovered refresh_url field in the POST /auth/login response and tested refreshing an active token.
findings.impact: Allows client sessions to stay authenticated seamlessly beyond the 15-minute access token lifespan.

findings.documented: Endpoints are accessible with only an API key scoped to your city.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings, /v1/rentals, and /v1/projects return 401 'missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first' if called without an Authorization: Bearer <token> header.
findings.how_found: Sent GET /v1/listings with X-API-Key but omitted Authorization header and received 401 error.
findings.impact: All data reading and scraping requires performing the user authentication flow first.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page and limit. page is 1-indexed, limit default 20, max 200. Response: { total, page, page_size, results }.
findings.actual: Collection endpoints completely ignore 'page' and instead use 'offset' and 'limit'. Response envelope contains { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results } with no 'page' or 'page_size' fields.
findings.how_found: Requested page=2 and observed offset: 0 and page 1 items returned; passing offset=50 properly returned the next slice.
findings.impact: Clients relying on page parameters will endlessly fetch the first page; pagination must use offset.

findings.documented: limit default 20, maximum 200.
findings.actual: Server hard-caps limit to a maximum of 50 records per request. Any limit requested above 50 (e.g. 100, 200) returns 50 records with limit: 50 in response.
findings.how_found: Requested limit=100 and limit=200; observed response returned exactly 50 records with response limit: 50.
findings.impact: Ingestion and browsing require 4x more requests than documented to paginate full collections.

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters. To fetch every record, read total, divide by your limit, and request that many pages.
findings.actual: Response total is severely underreported: listings reports total: 4301 but has 4700 retrievable records; rentals reports 1739 but has 1900; projects reports 476 but has 520.
findings.how_found: Iterated with offset until has_more was false, retrieving 4700 listings instead of the reported 4301.
findings.impact: Applications terminating pagination based on total miss hundreds of valid listings and projects.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns inactive listings as well; 978 out of 4,700 listings have is_live: false, which was not documented.
findings.how_found: Inspected response objects and discovered the is_live boolean property with 978 false values.
findings.impact: Frontend must explicitly filter is_live === true to avoid displaying off-market or withdrawn properties to users.

findings.documented: Supports min_price (int, inclusive) and max_price (int, inclusive) query parameters.
findings.actual: min_price and max_price query parameters are accepted by the server but silently ignored; response returns all listings regardless of price.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?min_price=10000000&max_price=15000000 and received listings priced at 27.4M, 17.4M, 7.5M.
findings.impact: Price range filtering cannot be performed server-side and must be executed in client-side state.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: The project_id query parameter is silently ignored on /v1/listings, returning all city listings instead of filtering to the project.
findings.how_found: Called /v1/listings?project_id=P10001 and received total: 4301 with non-matching and null project IDs.
findings.impact: Filtering listings by builder project must be performed client-side.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} - A single listing.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found at singular /v1/listing/{id}. The active endpoint is plural: GET /v1/listings/{id}.
findings.how_found: Tested GET /v1/listing/MAG-1002627 (404) and GET /v1/listings/MAG-1002627 (200).
findings.impact: Detail view requests fail unless routing to the plural /v1/listings/{id}.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings/MAG-1002627/similar with valid authentication.
findings.impact: Similar listing recommendations must be computed client-side.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body { id: '...' }, DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found. The active endpoints are GET /v1/saved, POST /v1/saved with body { listing_id: '...' }, and DELETE /v1/saved/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Tested British and American spellings; discovered /v1/saved is the functional endpoint.
findings.impact: Favourites functionality fails completely unless using /v1/saved with listing_id payload key.

findings.documented: Endpoint is documented under the name /v1/favourites taking { id: '...' }.
findings.actual: POST /v1/saved requires JSON body { listing_id: '...' }. Passing { id: '...' } returns 422 Unprocessable Entity.
findings.how_found: Sent POST /v1/saved with { id: ... } and received 422 validation error indicating 'listing_id' is required.
findings.impact: Saving listings requires conforming to the undocumented { listing_id } payload schema.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found. No city analytics endpoint is implemented on the server.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/analytics/summary and related variations with valid auth; all returned 404.
findings.impact: Insights and dashboard screens must calculate market aggregates directly from listings and rental data.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees integer (Conventions: 'Money: Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API').
findings.actual: Project price_min and price_max are floating point values where numbers < 10 represent Crores (e.g. 1.04 Cr = 10,400,000 INR) and numbers >= 10 represent Lakhs (e.g. 99.8 L = 9,980,000 INR), never raw INR.
findings.how_found: Inspected project price values (ranging from 1.0 to 99.8) and compared with actual unit listing prices in the same projects.
findings.impact: Project UI displays incorrect pricing (e.g. Rs 1.04 instead of Rs 1.04 Crore) unless properly converted to INR.

findings.documented: Conventions: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: For website 'magichomes', 389 listings report carpet_area in square meters (< 300, e.g. 76, 82, 154) rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Analyzed area distribution across all portals; found areas < 300 exclusively on magichomes matching 1 sq m = 10.7639 sq ft.
findings.impact: Price per sqft calculations and unit displays are heavily skewed unless square meters are converted to square feet.

findings.documented: Conventions: Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Listings posted_at timestamps lack the 'Z' UTC suffix and carry no timezone offset (e.g. '2026-06-15T02:33:00'), while rentals use 'Z' and /health uses '+05:30'.
findings.how_found: Inspected posted_at across all retrievable listings.
findings.impact: Timestamps can be misconstrued as local time by parsers expecting standard UTC strings.

findings.documented: total_listings is the number of listings currently available in the project. It is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: total_listings disagrees with the actual number of active listings for 127 projects.
findings.how_found: Counted active listings grouped by project_id and compared against project total_listings.
findings.impact: Users see conflicting inventory numbers on project details versus listing search results.

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to exactly one physical property and is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: Contains 40 physically impossible records: negative prices, floor greater than total floors, carpet area greater than super built-up area, swapped latitude/longitude coordinates (lat > 50 in Arctic Russia), and 0-bedroom/0-bathroom apartments.
findings.how_found: Ran comprehensive integrity validation on physical constraints across all 4,700 listings.
findings.impact: Displays corrupted or physically impossible real estate records to users and corrupts statistical models.

findings.documented: Returns genuine active sale listings in your city.
findings.actual: Contains 8 fake listings with minuscule clickbait prices (Rs 6,250 to Rs 16,790 for full 2BHK/3BHK apartments) posted solely to attract leads and generate enquiries.
findings.how_found: Queried listings with sale prices under Rs 50,000.
findings.impact: Deceives property buyers with unrealistic bait prices and corrupts price statistics.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Cross-portal duplicates exist where multiple portals list the same physical unit (same apartment, locality, floor, total floors, bedrooms, and facing). 4,700 records represent only 4,182 distinct physical properties.
findings.how_found: Deduplicated records using composite key of apartment name, locality, floor, total floors, bedroom count, and facing direction.
findings.impact: Buyers encounter duplicate listings of identical properties across different brokers and portals.
